Descriptive Tables by Trial and Treatment Arm

nice_trial_table1.Rd

Builds descriptive summaries separately for each trial and treatment arm from pooled individual participant data, as used in multi-trial analyses such as trial-level surrogate endpoint studies. Each trial is summarized with nice_SMD_table1, so all conventions (denominators, missing values, weighting, SMDs) are identical; this function arranges the per-trial results into one table with a common set of rows. The result prints in the console, renders in Quarto and R Markdown, and exports to Word.

Usage

nice_trial_table1(
  dat, trial, treatment, covar_names = NULL, print_covariate_names = NULL,
  treatment_for_SMD = NULL, treatment_order = NULL, trial_order = NULL,
  layout = "wide", show_smd = TRUE, continuous_stats = "both",
  catDigits = 1, contDigits = 2, smdDigits = 3, categorical_vars = NULL,
  weights = NULL, weightDigits = 1, show_missing = "if_any",
  title = "Table 1 by trial and treatment", docx_path = NULL,
  notes = "full"
)

Arguments

dat

A data.frame, tibble, or data.table with one row per participant (individual participant data), containing the trial identifier, the treatment arm, the covariates, and optionally a weight column. Column names must be unique and nonempty.

trial

The trial identifier, given as a single column name in dat (for example "trial") or as a vector of length nrow(dat). Factors keep their level order for the display; other types use order of first appearance (override with trial_order). Rows with a missing trial are excluded with a warning.

treatment

The treatment arm, given as a single column name or a vector of length nrow(dat). Arms may differ between trials (for example a third arm in one trial). Rows with a missing treatment are excluded with a warning. Trials with fewer than two arms are omitted with a warning.

covar_names

Character vector of columns to summarize, in display order. Defaults to all columns other than the trial, treatment, and weight columns named by string. Select covariates explicitly when trial, treatment, or weights are supplied as external vectors.

print_covariate_names

Display labels, either an unnamed character vector with one label per entry of covar_names or a named vector named by all covariate names (any order). Defaults to the column names.

treatment_for_SMD

Character vector of length two naming the two arms whose SMD is reported within each trial, for example c("Placebo", "Active"). Defaults to the two arms of each trial when every trial has exactly two arms; required if any trial has more than two. If a trial lacks one of the named arms, its SMD is shown as an em dash and recorded as not estimable in smd.

treatment_order

Character vector listing every included treatment exactly once, giving the left-to-right (or top-to-bottom) order of arms within each trial. Defaults to factor level order or order of first appearance. A trial shows only the arms it contains.

trial_order

Character vector listing every included trial exactly once, giving the order of trials. Defaults to factor level order or order of first appearance. Use it, for example, to order trials by year or sample size.

layout

"wide" (default) or "long".

  • "wide": rows are variables (names bold, levels indented) and columns are trial blocks, each with one column per arm and optionally an SMD column, under a header spanning the trial name. Best for a few trials.

  • "long": rows are trial-by-arm combinations (with the arm size N and, for weighted tables, the sum of weights) and columns are variables; categorical variables get one column per level. This is the usual layout for many trials. SMDs are not shown in this layout; use x$smd.

show_smd

TRUE (default) or FALSE. Whether the wide layout includes a within-trial SMD column. Within a randomized trial baseline differences are chance imbalances, so many authors omit them; SMDs remain available in x$smd. Ignored for layout = "long".

continuous_stats

Which continuous summaries to display: "both" (default) for mean (SD) and median (Q1, Q3), "mean_sd", or "median_iqr". Display only; SMDs always use means and SDs. Using one statistic roughly halves the number of columns in the long layout.

catDigits

Integer 0 to 10. Decimal places for percentages. Default 1.

contDigits

Integer 0 to 10. Decimal places for means, SDs, medians, and quartiles. Default 2.

smdDigits

Integer 0 to 10. Decimal places for displayed SMDs. Default 3. Numeric SMDs in x$smd are not rounded.

categorical_vars

Optional character vector of covariates to treat as categorical, for example numeric stage codes. Factors, characters, and logicals are categorical automatically.

weights

Optional analysis weights, as a numeric column name or a numeric vector of length nrow(dat). Must be finite and nonnegative; rows with zero weight are excluded with a warning. Weights are applied within each trial and arm exactly as supplied. Survey design objects are not supported; use nice_SMD_table1 for each trial in that case.

weightDigits

Integer 0 to 10. Decimal places for weighted counts and sums of weights. Default 1.

show_missing

Controls Missing rows: TRUE/"always", FALSE/"never", or "if_any" (default here). With "if_any" a variable gets a Missing row if any trial has a missing value for it; trials with none show 0 (0.0%). See nice_SMD_table1.

title

Heading used when printing and in the Word document. Default "Table 1 by trial and treatment". Use "" to omit it.

docx_path

Optional new .docx filename. The table is written in landscape orientation; an existing file is never overwritten. For other options use save_table1_docx.

notes

Footnote style: "full" (default), "short", or "none". The short legend gives the cell layout, the SMD definition and the compared pair, NE, and lines for excluded rows, hidden Missing rows, omitted trials, or em dashes when applicable.

Details

Every statistic is computed within a trial and arm; nothing is pooled across trials. Rows follow a common structure: for categorical variables the levels are those observed in any trial, in the order of the data. A level not observed in a given trial displays as a zero count; an em dash marks a cell that does not apply (for example, a variable that is entirely missing in a trial, or an SMD whose arm pair is absent).

With many trials, a wide table is unreadable; use layout = "long", or split trials across several calls. A single trial-by-arm table is common in supplements of multi-trial individual participant data analyses; main-text tables often show only trial-level characteristics.

The per-trial nice_table1 objects are in x$trials, so any single trial can be printed or exported on its own.

Value

A nice_trial_table1 list with table (formatted data.frame), col_info (column keys, header labels, trial, arm, and type), row_info (row types for "wide"; trial and treatment for "long"), smd (long data.frame with one row per trial and variable: numeric SMD, status, reason), groups (per trial and arm raw counts, sums of weights, Kish effective sizes), trials (named list of nice_table1 objects), notes, settings, call, and flextable.

See also

nice_SMD_table1, table1_flextable, save_table1_docx, example_trial_data

Examples

d <- example_trial_data()
head(d)
#>     trial     arm age egfr    sex diabetes ckd_stage weight
#> 1 Trial A Placebo  55 35.5 Female       No        G3    1.0
#> 2 Trial A  Active  63 41.0   Male      Yes        G4    1.5
#> 3 Trial A Placebo  69 46.5 Female       No        G3    0.7
#> 4 Trial A  Active  NA 32.0   Male      Yes        G3    1.2
#> 5 Trial A Placebo  52 37.5   Male       No        G4    1.7
#> 6 Trial A  Active  60 43.0 Female       No        G3    0.9
table(d$trial, d$arm)
#>          
#>           Placebo Active High dose
#>   Trial A      30     30         0
#>   Trial B      24     24         0
#>   Trial C      24     24        24
vars <- c("age", "egfr", "sex", "diabetes", "ckd_stage")
labels <- c("Age (years)", "eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m2)", "Sex", "Diabetes", "CKD stage")

## ---- 1. Trials side by side (few trials) -----------------------------
## Trial C has three arms, so name the pair the SMD compares.
wide <- nice_trial_table1(
  d, trial = "trial", treatment = "arm", covar_names = vars,
  print_covariate_names = labels,
  treatment_for_SMD = c("Placebo", "Active")
)
wide

  d, "trial", "arm", vars, print_covariate_names = labels,
  treatment_for_SMD = c("Placebo", "Active"),
  layout = "long", continuous_stats = "mean_sd", notes = "short"
)

## ---- 3. Manuscript style: no SMD column, short legend ----------------
nice_trial_table1(
  d, "trial", "arm", vars, print_covariate_names = labels,
  treatment_for_SMD = c("Placebo", "Active"),
  show_smd = FALSE, notes = "short"
)

## ---- 4. Missing rows ---------------------------------------------------
## Only age and eGFR have missing values: "if_any" (default) shows Missing
## rows for them; "never" hides all; "always" shows one for every variable.
for (mode in c("if_any", "never", "always")) {
  x <- nice_trial_table1(d, "trial", "arm", vars,
                         treatment_for_SMD = c("Placebo", "Active"),
                         show_missing = mode)
  cat(mode, ":", sum(x$row_info$type == "missing"), "Missing rows\n")
}
#> if_any : 2 Missing rows
#> never : 0 Missing rows
#> always : 5 Missing rows

## ---- 5. Orders and labels ---------------------------------------------
nice_trial_table1(
  d, "trial", "arm", c("age", "sex"),
  print_covariate_names = c(sex = "Sex", age = "Age (years)"),
  treatment_for_SMD = c("Placebo", "Active"),
  trial_order = c("Trial C", "Trial A", "Trial B"),
  treatment_order = c("Active", "Placebo", "High dose")
)$groups
#>     trial treatment  n sum_weights effective_n
#> 1 Trial C    Active 24          24          24
#> 2 Trial C   Placebo 24          24          24
#> 3 Trial C High dose 24          24          24
#> 4 Trial A    Active 30          30          30
#> 5 Trial A   Placebo 30          30          30
#> 6 Trial B    Active 24          24          24
#> 7 Trial B   Placebo 24          24          24

## ---- 6. Rounding, categorical codes, grouping vectors ----------------
nice_trial_table1(
  d, d$trial, d$arm, c("age", "ckd_stage"),
  treatment_for_SMD = c("Placebo", "Active"),
  contDigits = 1, catDigits = 0, smdDigits = 2
)

  d, "trial", "arm", c("age", "sex"), weights = "weight",

  layout = "long"

save_table1_docx(wide, path, landscape = TRUE, font_size = 9)
